ἐγγίζω is a denominal verb formed from ἐγγύς with the verbalizing -ίζω, so rule 66's denominal clause and rule 104's φλογίζω → setteth on fire put the head on the word that glosses the root: draweth answers to no element of the lexeme and nigh spells ἐγγυ-. That keeps the chapter consistent with 21:8 and 21:20, where the same lexeme's is at hand heads on hand, and with rule 71's ἐγγύς → at hand. Heading on draweth remains the competing reading, on the ground that draw nigh reads as an ordinary verb phrase.

review_notes: Corrected the head of ἐγγίζει from draweth to nigh. ἐγγίζω is denominal from ἐγγύς, so draweth is the empty support verb and nigh carries the lexeme; rule 66's denominal clause (ἱκανώσαντι → made … meet on meet) and rule 104's φλογίζω → setteth on fire on fire decide it, and rule 24's habit requires the same analysis as 21:8 and 21:20, which head is at hand on hand.
Both articles are emptied by possessives belonging to their own ὑμῶν tokens under rule 20; neither pronoun is spent elsewhere, so rule 76 does not arise.
Neither imperative has an expressed preposition answering to its preverb, so up stays inside each verb's own unit under rule 106.
